Overview.text:
The Ghoul has been pushed to his limits and he's hungry for more.

His personal Perks, Hex: Nothing but Misery, Forever Entwined, and None Are Free, help him to Hinder Survivors, hook them more quickly, and block Windows and Pallets when all Generators are completed.

Lore.text:
Ken Kaneki was a gentle and kind-hearted boy who lived a simple life, studying literature at Kamii University, before a chance encounter turned his life upside down.

He and his friend Hide frequented the café Anteiku, where one of the regulars caught his eye: Rize Kamishiro. She shared his passion for reading, and he spotted her even reading the same novel as him. He worked up the courage to ask her on a date. While walking her home, Rize showed her true colors: those of a ghoul known as The Binge Eater. She feasted on his flesh, nearly killing him, until a freak construction accident caused her demise, and nearly caused his as well.

To save his life, doctors transplanted Rize's organs into Kaneki. He survived the surgery, but something was wrong... food lost its flavor, and strange cravings dogged him. The life-saving surgery had made him part-ghoul.

Confused and afraid, he followed his instincts into an alleyway where he ran into Touka Kirishima, one of the staff members at Anteiku. Shocked at his transformation, she brought him back to the café. He was surprised to learn that the staff at Anteiku were ghouls. They took him under his wing, helping him adapt to his new reality. He learned how to fight with his newfound powers, how to deal with his urges to kill and eat human flesh, and how to stay one step ahead of the CCG. His adaptation to his new life was cruelly interrupted when he was kidnapped and subjected to unprecedented physical and mental torture at the hands of a particularly cruel ghoul named Jason. His captor's exercises of control and profound violence were so diabolical that they broke Kaneki's mind, stripped him of what once made him human. His sense of self was shattered, and Rize stepped into the empty space, encouraging him to take control in his own life.

And control is what he took, paying back Jason's violence in kind. He broke free and battled his captor. The torture made him numb to pain, and his shattered psyche left him no space for hesitation. He defeated Jason after a short battle, and he devoured him.

He had been dragged into a nightmare a tormented boy, but he walked out a powerful ghoul. He considered what this would mean as he pushed his way through the heavy doors, and barely noticed as a black fog pooled around his feet. He walked out, confident that the torture was over. But as he observed his surroundings, he realized that perhaps it had only begun.

Trivia.text:
General

The Ghoul is the first character to be added to come from a Manga/Anime media that isn't a cosmetic for an existing character. Ken Kaneki also marks the first time in Dead By Daylight history where the killer is the main protagonist of the series. The Ghoul is the first Killer to date who does not have weapon that is one of his three Cosmetic slots. In-game, he uses his Kagune (the tentacles) for both Basic Attacks and Special Attacks. While there are others Killers without a weapon as such — like The Nemesis using his fist or The Dark Lord his hand — they at least featured that body part as a weapon Cosmetic, whereas The Ghoul does not. His cosmetic slots mirror that of survivors, having one for his head, torso and legs. The Ghoul Lore outlines the events of the first season of the Tokyo Ghoul anime. His appearance, however, reflects the second season. He would eventually receive the outfit from where he is taken from the final episode of the anime. The finger-cracking Kaneki does in some animations (e.g. idling in the menu, cool-down phase after a Basic Attack ), is a habit that he mirrored from Jason after the latter tortured him in Tokyo Ghoul. The Ghoul is the first killer to feature a quick time event in their gameplay. When initiating a grab attack, the player has the opportunity to perfectly time an input to be rewarded with an extension to their Enraged Mode Countdown. There is no penalty for failing the quick time event. The Ghoul is the first Killer to date with a unique Power Token removal feature upon breaking Pallets normally. When The Ghoul breaks a Pallet while Kagune Leap is not on cool-down, it enters a cool-down of the equivalent of 1 Power Token use (or 2 while in Enraged Mode). This was meant to alleviate a problematic tactic where The Ghoul could quickly catch up to Survivors having little to no time to approach the nearest resource, although this system is flawed and can be worked around by breaking a Pallet right before Kagune Leap leaves its cool-down. When using the cosmetic set "Awakened Ghoul", Kaneki's voice becomes clearer, since it removes his mask. The Ghoul's mori is a reference to Yamori's s defeat in the season final of season 1, where Kaneki stabs both of his hands, restraining him before he devoured his Kagune. The associated achievement name "Remember Who I Am" is a direct reference to the last line of the lyrics in the opening song of Season 1, Unravel.

Adaptation from Source

According to Dave Richards, Creative Director of Dead by Daylight, their reimagining of Ken Kaneki had to undergo a drastic change in personality to suit his role as a Killer: "Rather than making him a Survivor, as his moral compass in the series may suggest, we felt it would be more interesting to really lean into the horror and present an alternate reality where Kaneki became exactly what he feared. While such a drastic change to Ken Kaneki's personality was necessary to suit his role as a Killer, it allowed the team to delve into a Ghoul’s powers and take them to their darkest possible conclusion. Luckily, the Tokyo Ghoul Production Committee was on board for the story we wanted to tell, sharing our excitement to see this terrifying take on their protagonist." [ 1 ]

Cosmetics

Default Outfit is taken from the first episode of Season 2 when Kaneki joins Aogiri. Awakened Ghoul is taken from the final episode of Season 1 when Kaneki accepts himself as a Ghoul. Rize Kamishiro originates from Season 1 Episode 1.

Voice Lines

The Ghoul is the tenth Killer with voice-lines. The Ghoul is voiced by Ken Kaneki's original voice actor in the anime, Natsuki Hanae. "May I ask what your name is?" and "What are you going to do now?" lobby voice lines were originally meant to be used for finding survivors inside lockers.

Voice Line References

"What's one thousand minus seven?", said while performing a Memento Mori, is a reference to a mantra intended to keep Kaneki sane during his torture, instructing him to loudly count backwards from one thousand in increments of seven. "All of the liabilities of this world are due to the inadequacies of the person involved." is a quote from Jason. "It's my turn." is a quote from Kaneki in his fight with Jason. "I am... a ghoul." is a quote from Kaneki when he awakens to his ghoul-self. "May I ask what your name is?" is a quote from Kaneki during his confrontation with Amon in the second season.

power.name: One-Eyed Terror
power.description:
SPECIAL ABILITY: ONE-EYED TERROR The Ghoul starts the Trial with 2 Tokens. SPECIAL ABILITY: KAGUNE LEAP Press and hold the Power button to charge a Kagune Leap, while aiming the reticule at any vertical surface or Survivor within 14 metres. Press the Attack button to initiate a Kagune Leap, consuming -1 Token, or release the Power button to cancel it:

Attaches the tentacles to the target and quickly pulls The Ghoul forwards. Grants the ability to leap over Windows or dropped Pallets.

After performing a Kagune Leap, if there is still a Power Token available, a window of opportunity opens for 5 seconds:

Press the Attack button to initiate another Kagune Leap. Press the Secondary Power button to cancel the Power. The button may also already be pressed at any point during the Leap to instantly cancel it upon landing.

Kagune Leap automatically enters its cool-down after any of the following:

The last Power Token has been consumed. The window of opportunity has elapsed. A Vaulting action has been performed. A Survivor has been grabbed.

During the cool-down, Kagune Leap recharges all consumed Power Tokens at a speed of 4 seconds per Token. The Power only becomes available again after fully recharging all Tokens.

If Kagune Leap is not already on cool-down, breaking a Pallet causes it to enter a forced cool-down equivalent to 1 Power Token. SPECIAL INTERACTION: TARGETING SURVIVORS Targeting a Survivor and colliding with them directly during a Kagune Leap has multiple possible effects and interactions:

If it is the first Leap, indicated by the reticule showing a closed mouth, the Survivor will remain unharmed. If it is the second Leap, indicated by the reticule showing an open mouth, grants the ability to perform a Grab-Attack

SPECIAL ATTACK: GRAB-ATTACK While the Grab-Attack occurs automatically when the conditions are met, it features an optional button prompt QTE:

Swiftly press the Attack button to perfectly time the attack, extending the subsequent Countdown. Missing the button prompt will apply the regular Countdown.

The Grab-Attack applies the following effects to the targeted Survivor:

Applies the Injured State when healthy. Causes them to suffer from the Deep Wound Status Effect. Applies the Kagune Mark. Blocks the Exit Gates for the duration of the Grab-Attack. This effect lingers for 5 seconds after they are released.

After performing a Grab-Attack, The Ghoul enters Enraged Mode. SPECIAL AFFLICTION: KAGUNE MARK Fully Mending or entering the Dying State removes the Kagune Mark for that Survivor.

Marked Survivors cannot be injured by Grab-Attacks, but still suffer its other effects. SPECIAL MODE: ENRAGED MODE While in this mode, The Ghoul is granted these following effects:

Increases the number of Power Tokens to 3. Reduces the Power Recharge time to 2.5 seconds per Token. Reduces the Vaulting time while targeting a Survivor located across it. Increases the Pallet-breaking penalty to 2 Power Tokens.

Enraged Mode remains active for as long as there is at least one Survivor with the Kagune Mark or if the Countdown is active. SPECIAL INTERACTION: COUNTDOWN Once the last marked Survivor removes their Kagune Mark, the Countdown triggers and is indicated on their HUD Portrait.

The Countdown lasts for 40 seconds, after which Enraged Mode ends. Performing a perfectly timed Grab-Attack increases its duration to 50 seconds.

Overview.text:
A monstrosity of flesh and metal, Springtrap’s bloodstained past is littered with the innocent dead. His horrifying innovations are a reminder that beneath the cruelty lies a brilliant inventor, whose creations brought laughter and screams to the same unfortunate audience.

The Animatronic always comes back.

His personal Perks, Help Wanted, Phantom Fear, and Haywire, help him compromise Generators, make Survivors scream, and regress Exit Gate Switches.

Lore.text:
Deep within the abandoned Freddy Fazbear's Pizza, William Afton ran from the ghosts of his victims. He frantically put on his beloved Spring Bonnie costume, the disguise he wore while committing his heinous crimes, to hide from the pursuing spirits.

But fate had different plans for Afton. Something activated the springlocks within the Spring Bonnie costume. Metal clamped against metal, piercing the murderer and trapping him in his costume. As he screamed, the checkerboard floor rose up to meet him, and everything went black.

Thus was Springtrap born: from the death of a murderer.

He awoke to a familiar sound, his body a pillar of agony. The ghosts that had tormented him were gone. The walls surrounding him were decomposing, the floor beneath him failing away in mouldy patches. How much time had transpired since the springlocks tore through his body and fixed him within his costume? The urge to kill lingered within him still, the thirst long left unquenched.

The sound filled his ears again, Children`s laughter. Were children playing in the kitchen? Springtrap rose to his feet, adjusting to his new body, and marched towards the sounds.

He picked up speed as he moved. Walking turned to running. He rushed into the kitchen and found,

Nothing.

No children, no games, no laughter. Just a swirling mass of black fog enveloping the far wall.

Springtrap examined the fog. Curiosity tightened his grip on him as he stared into the darkness, his distended eyes could see shapes emerge within the fog.

Who were they? It didn`t matter. They were his victims now. Somehow, he knew the hunt could go on forever.

All he had to do was step into the fog.

Trivia.text:
General

The Animatronic was the fifth video game licensed Killer featured in Dead by Daylight. The Animatronic is the second Killer with a Power that allows him to immediately grab Survivors that is separate from a basic grab. The Animatronic is the first Killer to feature 2 unique intro animations in the lobby. The Animatronic's design in Dead by Daylight retains many details from his origin franchise with subtle changes for the game; On his body, he lacks the original black button on his chest, as well as the darker color patterns on his stomach, ears, waist and legs. On his head he misses his jaw springlocks that pierced his cheeks, but did return in his Blighted Springtrap cosmetic. William Afton's decayed corpse is present inside the suit as opposed to in the Five Nights at Freddy's series, where only his head and intestines were visible. For Dead by Daylight, William's arms and legs are severed at the elbow and ankles, respectively. His lore references multiple different parts of Five Nights at Freddy's 3: The first 3 lines reference his death and rebirth as seen at the end of Night 5; being chased by the ghosts of his victims until being forced into a springlock animatronic suit, that then malfunctions and kills him. The 5th line references the audio lure, a gameplay mechanic that involves luring Springtrap around Fazbear's Fright using an audio sample of a child's laughter. This lure was presumably used by the Entity to lure William to The Fog, as his lore takes place before he was brought to Fazbear's Fright. Prior to Dead By Daylight, William Afton was not depicted with a Fire Axe in any official media, or a Pizza Knife, but a standard kitchen knife in the graphic novels and the movie. The choice for a Fire Axe in Dead By Daylight might be informed design, since the character is associated with burning buildings. The overall visuals of the Fire Axe reflect this. The Fire Axe could also be a direct reference to fan content, with William Afton wielding a Fire Axe In The Living Tombstone's Five Nights at Freddy's 3 music video titled "Die in a fire" in which he uses it to dismember the main 4 animatronics in the series. This animation is a more plausible rendition of the Five Nights at Freddy's 3 minigame where William Afton dismembers them by hand. This could make sense considering the events of the minigame and animation take place right before William Afton gets springlocked which leads to Afton finding the Fog after waking up, possibly bringing the axe with him. The pizza knife could very likely be to make his weapon stand out more as Michael Myers and Chucky both use a kitchen knife, as well as to make the kitchen knife exclusive to the Yellow Rabbit.

Character Memes

One of his voicelines ("I'm the fun one!") has become very popular and iconic among the community and content creators, and since then has been used in a variety of videos, audios and posts.

Cosmetics

All of Springtrap's skins originate and are inspired by the Five Nights at Freddy's franchise and characters. Default Outfit is taken directly from Five Nights at Freddy's 3 (2015), although with some changes. Toxic Springtrap and Clown Springtrap are both from Five Nights at Freddy's AR: Special Delivery, a now defunct mobile game. Toxic Springtrap was given a slight redesign for his appearance in Dead by Daylight, featuring a more bloated appearance. Clown Springtrap features make up in William Afton's face. The description of the cosmetic piece makes note that Afton does not recognise the make-up or clothes he wears, implying they were forced onto him by The Entity. Clown Springtrap had his proportions altered so that it would fit Springtrap's rig. Blighted Springtrap features heavy inspiration from Scraptrap from Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria Simulator and Burntrap from Five Nights at Freddy's Security Breach. Scraptrap's inspiration can be seen with the skull having an exposed brain and the suit's head featuring a bent jaw. Burntrap's inspiration can be seen with the more exposed corpse, clawed hands (One of which has growing flesh where Burntrap's hands had flesh attached to it), a metallic spine and the third hand doing the arm crawl that can be seen in his first appearence during his boss fight in Security Breach. Yellow Rabbit is taken directly from William Afton's appearance in the live action Five Nights at Freddy's movie, with Matthew Lillard reprising his role through both voice and likeness in Dead by Daylight. His starting animation is a reference to his entrance in the movie wearing the costume. When loading into a Trial, one can see him holding his left side of his belly. This is where the springlocks had activated when he was attacked by the Cupcake. Yellow Rabbit has voice lines towards Nicolas Cage, making him the third killer since Chucky to have the voice lines toward the actor. Glitchtrap originates from Five Nights at Freddy's: Help Wanted, serving as the main antagonist. Glitchtrap intro is a reference to the Pizza Party ending, where he waves at the player and lures them to get stuffed inside Freddy Fazbear, while dancing in the background. Glitchtrap is the second Legendary since Rize Kamishiro to feature a slightly altered Mori animation as instead of jumpscaring, he shushes at the survivor. Glitchtrap has unique Grab Axe and Security Door Travel Jumpscare animations. When he grabs his axe, instead of jumpscaring, he will shush at the Survivor. When he catches a Survivor while traveling in the office, instead of immediately running towards the survivor he will wave at them and pull out a knife behind his back after grabbing a survivor. Glitchtrap' s current identity is unknown with hints that it is William Afton who returned from his demise in Freddy Fazbear's pizzeria simulator (Or potentially a creature made from his agony) or Mimic1 (F10-N4)/Mimic2 (The Mimic) copying William posthumously (The existence of a third Mimic made to copy William is also possible) or a mix of both (Being that William Afton or his agony is possessing at least some part of either of the Mimics's programming), but for now none of those theories are confirmed and will be treated as such until direct confirmation of Glitchtrap's identity is given. Originally a digital manifestation within Five Nights at Freddy's: Help Wanted, the flavour text for the cosmetic states that the Entity had transformed Glitchtrap into a physical being. While sitting idle in the lobby, Glitchtrap will occasionally jumpscare unsuspecting players. After this sequence ends he teleports back with a glitch effect. Up until 9.1.1 Patch, the effect would use Toba Landing 's colony logo, likely as a placeholder. Glitchtrap shares voice actor with The Nemesis, The Xenomorph Were-Elk, Leshen and some of the wailing voices behind The Dredge.

Easter Eggs

The Animatronic features two unique Lobby Animations when selecting him; The Animatronic may enter the screen from the left before walking out of frame. The Animatronic will grab the side of the screen, glaring at the player before disappearing. Both of the above lobby animations are references to Five Nights at Freddy's 3, as these are how Springtrap enters the office to kill the player. The Animatronic's power name, Fazbear's Fright, is a direct reference to the location of the same name that Five Nights at Freddy's 3 takes place in. Coincidently, there is a short story book series of a similar name; Fazbear Frights. The perk Phantom Fear may be a reference to a jumpscare mechanic in Five Nights at Freddy's 3, in which looking at some of the Phantom Animatronic will jumpscare the player. The jumpscares in both his Mori and when grabbing the Fire Axe may also reference this, as the Phantom Animatronics will scream in the player's face when jumpscaring them. The Animatronic's idle animation in both the Lobby and in a Trial is identical to his official render in Five Nights at Freddy's 3 after completing the game, where you can view not only Springtrap, but the other Phantom Animatronics. While in the Lobby, The Animatronic may convulse and grab his head screaming before returning to his normal idle stance. The way he grabs his head is similar to the hidden screenshots that may appear when starting up a game or dying in Five Nights at Freddy's 3. The Animatronic's official store render in Dead by Daylight is very similar to his official render for his appearance in Five Nights at Freddy's AR: Special Delivery. The Animatronic's weapon clean animation after a Basic Attack is a reference to the same action from the live action Five Nights at Freddy's movie, which in turn was a nod to the Scream franchise, as Matthew Lillard played one of the two original Ghostfaces in addition to William Afton. The Endoskeleton featured in The Animatronic's Mori is a reference to the Five Nights at Freddy's movie, referencing the Freddy head that was modified with sawblades to kill its victims while they were trapped in a chair, and it was later used to attack the protagonist Mike Schmidt. This Endoskeleton is also present in the Parts and Service Room within Freddy Fazbear's Pizza also tied in a chair. Entering Supply Closet will cause an Endoskeleton to pop out of a vent in the ceiling. This is likely a reference to both Five Nights at Freddy's 2 and 3 where the Animatronics, including Springtrap, will traverse the Pizzeria and later Fazbear's Fright through the vents in the buildings. When sitting in the lobby looking at the Survivors, The Animatronic may turn slightly and look at the screen. The way he does this is similar to the way he looks at the security guard through the cameras in one of the vents in Five Nights at Freddy's 3. The icon for the achievement "None the Wiser" is a direct reference to the graphic novel artwork for the Fazbear Frights story: What We Found. The Horror Attraction Banner features Springtrap appearing in the window of the office in Fazbear's Fright which is a reference to Five Nights at Freddy's 3 where Springtrap can stare at the player from the window in the office. The "Vent Crawl" banner features Springtrap crawling in the ventilations which is a reference to Five Nights at Freddy's 3 but also Five Nights at Freddy's: Help Wanted as you could see Springtrap crawling his way through the ventilation to the office before he jumpscares the player. The Score Event for a Survivor entering the area of effect of the Fire Axe is called "Look at You", which is likely a reference to the monologue William Afton/Yellow Rabbit gives at the end of the first movie when confronted by the main four animatronics.

Voice Lines

Most of The Animatronic' s voice lines are references to his quotes in the games Five Nights at Freddy's AR: Special Delivery and Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria Simulator. However, some of his lines are taken from other characters from Ultimate Custom Night and Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria Simulator. His iconic catchphrase "I always come back" is a reference to the Five Nights At Freddy's 3 teaser trailer, which contains the lines "He will come back; he always does", as well as being a line spoken by him in Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria Simulator, Ultimate Custom Night, and the Five Nights at Freddy's movie. "The darkest pit of hell is open for business" is a reference to a line delivered by Henry Emily in one of the endings of Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria Simulator. ("Although for one of you, the darkest pit of hell has opened to swallow you whole, so don't keep the Devil waiting, old friend.") "You will not be spared, you will not be saved" and "I am here to claim what is left of you" are taken from his quotes in Five Nights at Freddy's AR: Special Delivery, which are in turn directly taken from Nightmare in Ultimate Custom Night. "Play with fire and you'll get burned" is taken and altered from Rockstar Foxy in Ultimate Custom Night. ("Y'arr, ya play with fire and sometimes ye get burned!") This line also serves as a reference to his fate at the end of both Five Nights at Freddy's 3 and Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria Simulator, where in both instances he gets lit on fire. "Lets pull you apart" is taken and slightly altered from Nightmare Fredbear in Ultimate Custom Night. ("Let's see how many times you can be pulled apart.") "It's me" is a recurring phrase in the series that is often associated with Golden Freddy, but has also been used by Glitchtrap, an alternate version of Springtrap, in Five Nights at Freddy's: Help Wanted. "Don't move." is a line spoken by William Afton in the Silver Eyes novel and its graphic novel after he removes the Spring Bonnie suit to reveal his springlock scars to Carlton.

power.name: Fazbear's Fright
power.description:
"The Animatronic lived to kill, even when his mechanical costume became his tomb." SPECIAL ABILITY: FAZBEAR'S FRIGHT The Animatronic is armed with a Fire Axe, that he can throw, and causes 7 Security Doors to spawn in the environment. SPECIAL ABILITY: FIRE AXE Press and hold the Power button to initiate Ready Aim. Press the Attack button to throw the Fire Axe or release the Power button to cancel the Power. If the Fire Axe hits a Survivor, the Survivor is damaged for one health state, and, if Healthy, has the Fire Axe embedded into them. Survivors with an embedded Fire Axe are inflicted with the Broken and Oblivious Status Effects. If the Fire Axe hits the environment, the Fire Axe becomes embedded and creates an Area of Effect of 2 metres around it. Any Survivors caught inside the area are revealed by Killer Instinct. If the Fire Axe hits a Security Door, the door becomes disabled for all Survivors until the Fire Axe is removed. SPECIAL INTERACTION: RECLAIM AXE While the Fire Axe is off cool-down, press the Secondary Power button to retrieve the Fire Axe. SPECIAL INTERACTION: GRAB AXE Press the Power button while infront of a Survivor with an embedded Fire Axe to perform a special sequence that instantly carries the Survivor and returns the Fire Axe to The Animatronic. SPECIAL MAP FEATURE: SECURITY SYSTEM The Security Doors found in the enviroment can be accessed by both Survivors and The Animatronic. Upon entering a Security Door, The Animatronic benefits from the following effect:

Grants the Undetectable Status Effect. This effect lingers for 20 seconds after travelling to an another Security Door.

SPECIAL INTERACTION: CAMERA VIEW Each Security Door has a Camera attached to it. Interacting with the door gives a Survivor access to the Camera View, allowing them to cycle through every Camera:

Survivors are able to travel to the selected Security Door by pressing the Secondary Action button Survivors are also able to reveal The Animatronic by looking at him through Camera View, doing so reveals his aura to all Survivors for 10 seconds and removes the Undetectable granted by Security Door travel.

SPECIAL MECHANIC: BATTERY POWER Using the Cameras and Security Doors will drain the battery power. Fully depleting the battery power shuts down the Security System for 45 seconds, forcing Survivors to wait until the system reboots. The Animatronic may travel between doors with or without battery power. SPECIAL LOCATION: SECURITY ROOM If The Animatronic enters a Security Door, they may choose to exit from any other door in the environment. Moving to a door already in use by a Survivor will cause The Animatronic to grab that Survivor.

Overview.text:
A shape-changing Killer, able to inflict Survivors with an effect that weakens them to her Intestinal Whip attack.

Her personal Perks, Ravenous, Wandering Eye, and Hex: Overture of Doom, help her increase mid-trial pressure, spot injured Survivors, and cause confusion to her whereabouts.

Lore.text:
Burong Sukapat's operatic rehearsals in Thailand were a sea of emotion, but despite tiring efforts she was unable to become anything more than an understudy. What started as a desire to share her gift, became an unshakable need for fame. Her childhood friend Janjira was her biggest supporter, but aside from a shoulder to cry on, there was little more she could offer. It wasn't until Malai—a fellow singer who had quickly risen the ranks—reached out, that Burong's fortunes changed.

Malai presented Burong with a glass bottle, a clear liquid within, and advised her to drink it, her tone deadly serious:

Each night, another will inhabit your body—but you will be a success on the stage like me.

Burong laughed at the peculiar game. Even so, she wanted more than anything to believe its truth. She grabbed the bottle, swallowing every drop.

In the following weeks, Burong's skin felt softer, and she found a depth in her voice she never knew existed. During her next audition, the director took notice, enraptured by the sound that echoed through the theatre. As the song ended, Burong thanked the director before coughing blood into a handkerchief. She stuffed it into her pocket, choosing ignorance. Whatever was happening to her was working—she wouldn't dare stop it now.

That night, as she slept, a soothing warmth dripped down her body. She bolted upright, hand fumbling for a lamp that wasn't there. She lay in a yard she did not recognize, covered in blood. Next to her, a ravaged chicken coop, feathers and gore staining the ground.

She stumbled home before the city awoke to a new day. Under a scalding shower, she spit up blood, dreading the thought that this hadn't been her first hunt. In between heaving sobs, she prodded her abdomen, searching for where something might hide within.

She called Janjira but couldn't bring herself to reveal the horrors, instead telling her friend she'd been restlessly sleepwalking each night and needed someone to coax her back to bed. Janjira agreed to help.

That morning, Burong awoke to Janjira's hand lovingly placed on her cheek. As she looked up, she choked on her cries. Janjira's severed hand fell from the bed, landing on her disembowelled carcass.

For hours, she sat beside her friend's remains in a state of silent shock. Janjira was dead and for what?

When she couldn't stand the smell of blood any longer, she grabbed cleaning supplies. As the sun set, a deep stain remained on the carpet.

She walked through the streets until she reached Malai's home. Malai opened the door and, upon seeing Burong's eyes, immediately defended herself. She claimed she had committed no wrong—she had been cursed, and the only way to be rid of it was to pass it to someone else. She believed that Burong, in her desire for fame, could withstand the torment and achieve what she'd always wanted.

Anger stirred within Burong. She fell to the floor as furious heat spilled over her. Malai stared in horror while Burong dug nails into her own skin, ripping at the burning agony. As she tore chunks of flesh from her neck, her entrails wriggled inside. Her head tore free from her body, a long string of organ dragging behind like fish slapping against the shore.

A seething hunger took over as Burong's disembodied head lifted into the air. It swooped at Malai, ravenously mutilating the woman until nothing remained but blood, hair, and bone. Burong awoke to the mess, unable to find the sympathy to shed a single tear.

She returned home, allowing her thoughts to swirl until the room filled with light.

The phone rang.

The director's voice cut through the haze that had settled on her mind. He offered her the leading role. Burong fell to her bed and cried, not from sadness, but from relief and elation.

During the evenings on the Bangkok stage, her star shined bright. At night, she fed the creature within, and together they thrived in a world of hunger and song. But the creature always wanted more and one night it was presented just that—a promise of meat, hung on hooks, dripping with tantalizing blood.

And then there was fog.

Trivia.text:
General

The Krasue is the third Killer to use a third-person camera since The Good Guy. However, The Krasue only uses it in Head Form, with her default Body Form using the regular first-person camera for Killers. She is, however, the first Killer to stay in third-person while carrying a Survivor in Head Form. The Krasue is the first killer to have two different animations for carrying survivors. In her Body Form, she simply hoists and carries them over her shoulder. In her Head Form, she lifts the Survivor by their necks via her intestines, akin to Killers like The Xenomorph. The Krasue is the first non-licensed killer to carry survivors this way. The Krasue's name in the promotional art is spelled as "บุรง", however the in-game lore localised in Thai shows the spelling as "บุหรง". Both renditions are most likely coming from a difference in localisation choices, as Burong can be spelled from, and localised into both words. During the PTB for Patch 9.2.0, the initial part of her description (the one before a Killer's Perks are mentioned) was less fleshed-out and simply read: The Krasue hungers for blood.

Voice Actress

The Krasue's Body Form is voiced by Organ, the preferred moniker of Dr Fueanglada Prawang Carlson, a professional opera singer and vocal instructor at the Voice Department of Mahidol University in Thailand. [ 1 ] Organ is featured in a short Meet the Voice video released on the official Dead by Daylight channel a few days after the Chapter's release (see Gallery ). The Krasue's Head Form is voiced by Roxana B.L. (The Monster Factory), who previously voiced the Female Zombie featured in Trials against The Nemesis and is also one of the many voices used to create the cacophonous wails and screams heard when facing The Dredge.

Voice Lines

The Krasue is the third Killer to speak any other contemporary language other than English, being Thai. She does speak English briefly in Lobby Voice Line 06.

power.name: Unbodied Flesh
power.description:
SPECIAL ABILITY: CORPOREAL WEAVE The Krasue can shift between Body Form and Head Form at will. Press the Secondary Power button to initiate a shift. SPECIAL SHAPE: BODY FORM The Krasue always starts the Trial in this state:

Regular Terror Radius of 32 metres. Regular Movement speed of 4.6 m/s. Grants access to the Regurgitate special ability.

SPECIAL SHAPE: HEAD FORM This Form provides The Krasue with the following effects and abilities:

Larger Terror Radius of 40 metres. Faster Movement speed of 4.8 m/s. Grants access to the Headlong Flight special ability. Grants access to the Intestinal Whip special attack. Replaces the ability to break dropped Pallets with the ability to vault across them. Vaulting times: Pallets: 1.9 seconds Windows: 1.67 seconds Longer Pallet Stun duration of 2.5 seconds. Disables the Bloodlust Status Effect.

SPECIAL AFFLICTION: LEECHED Hitting Survivors with a Leeching Gland or the Intestinal Whip fills their Leech Meter, indicated on their HUD portrait. Once the meter is full at 100 Charges, affected Survivors suffer from Leeched I:

Causes the Intestinal Whip attack to incur damage. Causes the Leech Meter to charge passively at a rate of +1.665 c/s.

If Survivors afflicted with Leeched I passively fill the Leech Meter a second time, they will suffer from Leeched II:

Healthy Survivors receive damage and become injured. Incurs the Broken Status Effect, regardless of their Health State.

SPECIAL ABILITY: REGURGITATE While in Body Form, press and hold the Power button to initiate the Charge Regurgitate interaction. Releasing the Power button will cancel it. Press the Attack button when fully charged to spew a Leeching Gland:

Rebounds off of environmental objects and splits into 4 smaller mini-glands that home-in on nearby Survivors. Adds +100 Charges to the Leech Meter of Survivors hit with either projectile-type, filling it completely. Cannot exeed Leeched I.

Regurgitate has a cool-down of 2.5 seconds. SPECIAL ABILITY: HEADLONG FLIGHT While in Head Form, with the Power Gauge filled to at least 25 %, press and hold the Power button to speed through the air at 7.0 m/s:

The Power Gauge has a capacity of 12 Charges. Flying depletes the Power Gauge at a rate of -1 c/s. The Power Gauge recharges at a rate of +0.4 c/s.

SPECIAL ATTACK: INTESTINAL WHIP While in Head Form, press the Attack button to lash out with your internal organs:

Ignores obstructions for the initial 0.35 seconds of the attack. Adds +34 Charges to the Leech Meter of hit Survivors, partially filling it. Cannot exceed Leeched I. Damages Survivors already afflicted with at least Leeched I.

SPECIAL ITEM: GLOWING FUNGUS The Glowing Fungus can be found randomly throughout the environment.

Can be eaten by Survivors afflicted with Leeched I to lower their Leeched Meter over time. This effect ends after being hit.

The Trial starts with 5 Glowing Fungi located throughout the environment, with a maximum of 6 able to exist at the same time. Glowing Fungi spawn under the following conditions, up to that limit:

Whenever The Krasue transitions from Body Form to Head Form while at least 5 metres away from any interactable object or other Glowing Fungi. After 90 seconds of consuming a Glowing Fungus by any means.

Overview.text:
The First is a cunning and cruel former test subject, whose powers were sharpened in an alternate dimension.

His personal Perks, Turn Back the Clock, Secret Project, and Hex: Hive Mind, allow him to damage distant Generators, block them from repair, and set them back when another is completed.

Lore.text:
From a young age, Henry Creel was disgusted by humanity and their endless cycles of eating, reproducing and dying. Their mindless play. As this hatred bubbled and fermented, he found that he had strange powers: first, an ability to control the house's grandfather clock, and later, the ability to manipulate minds. His powers reached a terrifying new level as he contorted and destroyed the bodies of his mother and sister. Henry's father, blamed for their deaths, was sent to Pennhurst Mental Hospital.

A shadowy organization faked Henry's death and moved him to a facility where his powers were limited by the Soteria chip, and studied along with several other children with psionic powers. He played along and was eventually made an orderly. But his compliance was a ruse. Once he was able to convince Eleven to remove his chip, he massacred the students and staff of the facility, only stopping when Eleven was able to banish him to another dimension.

Henry thought he was going to die. Instead, he became more powerful than ever before. From this new dimension, he committed a series of grisly murders as part of his plan to open gates to the real world and destroy all of humanity. But as he passed through a gate, a black fog appeared and he crossed over into a new realm - one unfamiliar, but full of potential.

Trivia.text:
General

Henry Creel's alias, Vecna, originates from The Lich, due to being nicknamed so by the cast of Stranger Things. He is loosely based on the character. [ 1 ] This is shared with The Demogorgon. Three of his voice-lines, "I will not be denied", "Enough games" and "Your time draws near", are shared with The Lich. Additionally, quite a few of The First's voice-lines are nearly identical to some voice-lines of The Lich, such as, "There is no escape", versus The Lich's "There will be no escape." The First shares his lobby theme with The Demogorgon and the Stranger Things survivors. The First is the first killer to share a menu theme with another killer outside of the default menu theme and cosmetic menu themes. The First was inspired by many classic horror villains. [ 2 ] The First's visuals and his methods of killing are inspired by Freddy Krueger. It was also partially inspired by Pinhead alongside his presence in the show. The First is also inspired by Pennywise from IT, due to him targeting his victims by using their fear as an exploitable weapon. The First was the first Killer to receive a portrait update from PTB to Live. Originally, it was more saturated and with higher contrast. Those were reversed at release. The associated achievement, "Torn Asunder", is likely a reference to the lyrics of a song used in Season 4, "Running Up That Hill" by Kate Bush, "Unaware I'm tearin' you asunder". The First is the first killer that cannot be rotated by the player while in the Store. The First's character portrait mirrors The Lich.

Character Memes

Due to being the second Killer named Vecna to be added to Dead by Daylight, Henry has been memed on endlessly by the community. This has led to several humorous remarks, such as naming him The Second - Vecna, or comparing him to The Lich, the latter being called "The Cooler Vecna", which was strengthened by Season 5's mixed reception. His title "The First" was also turned into a joke, due to the fact he is in the literal and in the meta sense not the first Vecna.

Cosmetics

All of The First's skins are taken from his appearances through the show. Henry Creel was worn by The First during the flashbacks of Season 4, when Henry worked as an orderly for Hawkins Laboratory (Season 4, Episode 5-7 & Season 5, Episode 4 & 5). Henry Creel is the third legendary since Rize Kamishiro to slightly alter the mori of the Killer. Instead of stabbing through his victims's skull, Henry levitates them with a hand gesture. Scion of The Upside Down was worn by The First during the flashbacks of Season 4, when Henry is sent to Dimension X by Eleven (Season 4, Episode 7) It was slightly altered so it features a precursor to his main Season 4 design with his clawed hand. Default Outfit originates from Season 5, being his true form. (Season 5, Episodes 4-8).

Lore

His lore depicts his origin story and the events of Season 4. However, his appearance is from Season 5. Despite the Mind Flayer appearing in the Stranger Things lobby, it is unknown whether it is the real thing or a manifestation of The Entity. The lore makes no mention of the Mind Flayer entering the Fog too, but could possibly have still entered the realm due its strong connection to Henry at the time of his entry.

Memento Mori

The First is the fourth killer to feature two entirely different Moris. His first Mori is his iconic method of killing his victims by stabbing them in the head with his clawed hand, lifting them up into the air, breaking their limbs and jaw and making their eyes pop out of their sockets. When he killed Chrissy in Season 4, it was a reference a reference to one of Freddy Krueger 's kills, from both the original and remake, where he kills Tina/Kris. His second Mori, Mindbreak, suspends the Survivors in the air, before twisting their neck backwards.

Voice Lines

The First is the eleventh Killer to actively speak during Trials. Peforming a Mori on Dustin Henderson, Eleven, Nancy Wheeler, and Steve Harrington along with their legendary outfits will trigger a special interaction where The First speaks to them by name and mocks them.

Voice Line References

Several of his voice lines are taken from Season 4 of Stranger Things, when Henry taunts his victims before killing them. In particular, "It's time for your suffering to end", "Join me", "Weak. Fragile" and "You. Will. Break".

power.name: Test Subject #001
power.description:
SPECIAL ABILITY: VINE ATTACK Press and hold Power button to start charging Vine Attack. Release the Power button button to cancel the Power. Press the Attack button while fully charged to create an area of effect on the ground, Survivors caught inside it will be inflicted 1 Worldbreaker Token. SPECIAL ABILITY: THE UPSIDE DOWN The First can enter The Upside Down by pressing the Secondary Power button. While in The Upside Down, The First:

Can peform Undergate Attack. Is granted Undetectable. Moves at 8 m/s. Ignores the collisions of: Breakable Walls, Pallets and Windows

This ability has a 35 second cool-down after exitting The Upside Down. At the start of the trial, the ability starts at 50% of the base cool-down. SPECIAL ABILITY: UNDERGATE ATTACK Press the Attack button to peform the Undergate Attack. Performing the attack causes an area of effect to grow around The First 's position. Once it reaches the full radius, The First exits The Upside Down. Any Survivors caught inside the radius of the attack are inflicted 2 Worldbreaker tokens. SPECIAL AFFLICTION: WORLDBREAKER & WORLDBREAKER TOKENS Survivors can be inflicted up to 4 Worldbreaker tokens. Worldbreaker is activated when:

Any Survivor reaches 2 or 4 Worldbreaker tokens. Any Survivor with 4 Worldbreaker tokens is hit by either Vine Attack or Undergate Attack.

While Worldbreaker is active, Vine Attack and Undergate Attack will inflict damage to Survivors instead of inflicting Worldbreaker tokens. Worldbreaker has two durations phases: Phase One and Phase Two. Phase One's duration is determined by the amount of Survivors present in the Trial: 60 seconds for each Survivor present in the Trial. Phase Two lasts for 50 seconds. Worldbreaker 's base count down is paused while carrying a Survivor. SPECIAL OBJECT: GRANDFATHER CLOCK 4 Grandfather Clocks spawn in the Trial. They become available to Survivors during Worldbreaker 's Phase One duration phase. Survivors are able to interact with Grandfather Clocks to speed up the count down of Phase One. SPECIAL INTERACTION: MIND BREAK Survivors who reached the second Hook Stage and have 4 Worldbreaker tokens become exposed to Mind Break. During Worldbreaker, if the Survivor exposed to Mind Break is inflicted damage that would send them to the Dying State by Vine Attack or Undergate Attack, the Survivor will be sent floating into the air. The First is able to perform the Mind Break Mini-Mori while standing next to the floating Survivor by pressing the Secondary Power button.

Overview.text:
No matter where you run, Jason is never far away. Relentless, vicious, and brutally creative, the masked slasher will never run out of inventive ways to kill. It’s all fun and games until a piece of scrap metal bursts through your chest.

The Slasher is the embodiment of horror, a relentless Killer who is always on the hunt.

His personal perks, Hex: Scared to Death, Silent Shadow, and Rampage, allow him to excel at chases, stealthily hunt Survivors, and recover after being stunned.

Lore.text:
The Slasher looms at edge of the treeline. On his face is an old, worn hockey mask, expressionless, a grave threat. Ahead is a tent, the silhouette of a camper within.

If it were any other misty night, the Greenville forest would be alive with the sounds of wildlife. Tonight, there is silence.He takes stock of anything useful scattered near the tent: rope, tent spikes, a hacksaw. Gripping his machete with a strength that could crush the handle, he steps from the shadows.

A quick swipe tears the tent open.

It’s not a camper that stares up at him. It is… something else. Almost human. Skin twisted and deformed in a familiar way. Mouth fixed in a perpetual grin. Covered in blood, holding an axe. There are signs of a struggle, yet no victim to be seen.The creature watches and waits, twitching with uncertainty. The Slasher stares back, fixated on its misshapen face.

“Can you help find my cat?” asks the creature, voice shifting between pitches. Without warning, it plants its axe into The Slasher’s chest.

The Slasher doesn’t hesitate. He reaches out and snaps the creature’s neck, wrenching it backwards.

It remains standing.

He stabs his machete into its belly. The creature’s head twists back into place. Moonlight reveals dark holes where its eyes should be.

A fleshy proboscis extends from its neck and opens.A booming force strikes The Slasher. He staggers, disoriented.

The creature’s axe cuts through his muscle, hits bone. The Slasher slams his hand forward, through the creature’s chest. His fist tightens around what feels like a beating heart.

He rips his hand out, holding not a heart but a clump of entangled flesh. The spidery thing crawls up his arm, stabbing with hooked protrusions. He rips it off, chunks of skin coming with it.

The creature seizes the advantage. Knocks him down, tosses the axe aside, and wails on him with surprising force. Ribs snap like dry wood.

The Slasher reaches for the hacksaw. He slashes it across the creature’s throat. Pink ooze spills onto his mask. The creature continues its assault. The Slasher scrapes the blade deeper, cutting through thick, sinewy flesh until the creature’s head falls from its body.

It writhes in the dirt, a desperate, violent, and ineffective movement. After a final thrash, it collapses, lying motionless.

The Slasher turns away, scores of wounds across his body, and strides into the darkness. A crimson trail follows his every step.Behind him, a warbling voice calls out.

“I could use a hand here.”

In a flash, the headless creature charges on all fours. Tentacles burst from a gaping maw on its back and seize The Slasher. Snapping jaws emerge, burrowing into his body. He spasms. Blood seeps from the holes of his mask. The moon’s glow darkens.

With one final push, The Slasher thrusts his fists through the worming appendages and into the maw. He rises to his feet, lifting the creature, impaling it on his arms. With an overpowering heave, he slams it into the ground.

Still, it moves. The Slasher grabs its legs and swings it into a tree. A sickening crunch. He swings again. He doesn’t stop until he holds in his hands two legs, unconnected to the fleshy puddle of gore that lies beneath him.

Something twitches in the puddle, as if thin threads of muscle twine back together. The Slasher looks around. The mist that permeates this forest turns black.

In the gloom, he glimpses visions of skittish, fearful people roaming the forests. He storms through the dark cloud, wisps parting to reveal a young woman, olive skinned, scarf around her neck. Her eyes widen in terror. He swings his machete.

Her screams are cut short as she chokes on the blood that spews from her throat. Her death echoes through the realm as a warning.

Jason is here.

Trivia.text:
General

The Slasher visually inspired The Trapper. The Slasher' s default design was inspired by his appearances from Friday the 13th Part 2 and Friday the 13th Part 3. The design also bears a resemblance from his appearances in Freddy vs Jason, Friday the 13th (2009) and the fighting game Mortal Kombat X, in which Jason makes a guest appearance. The Slasher' s default design and mask was designed by makeup artist Greg Nicotero, who is known for his work on The Walking Dead. He also designed a mask for the Scream version of Ghost Face before movie producers settled on the Fun World mask, and made an original design for Leatherface in the The Texas Chain Saw Massacre (2023) game published by Gun Interactive who also were the publisher behind the now defunct Friday The 13th: The Game. According to Behavior's Head of Partnerships, Mathieu Cote, Jason was one of the few licensed Killers that had an open invitation. The other Killer is Pennywise from It. Said invitation can be seen in his reveal trailer and the Sealed Letter Badge. The Slasher is the second Killer to feature unique Hooks when present in the Trial. The first was The Xenomorph. The Slasher is the first Killer to be able to destroy Hooks. The Slasher' s Add-ons include references from the first eight films from the Friday the 13th franchise, with all of them being references to iconic kills: Bent Wheel and Deputy's Badge Add-ons reference Friday the 13th Part 2. Knitting Needle, Bloody Magazine, Burnt Fuse, and Eye Goop Add-ons reference Friday the 13th: Part 3. Missing Corkscrew, Coroner's Coffee, Orderly's Shoe, Two Nails, and Garden Claw Add-ons reference Friday the 13th: The Final Chapter. Dirty Money, Bloody Smile and Imprinted Aluminum Add-ons reference Friday the 13th Part 6: Jason Lives. Party Noisemaker and Sleeping Bag Add-ons reference Friday the 13th Part 7: The New Blood. Toxic Waste, Mirror Shards (Omnipresent Evil), and Sauna Rock Add-ons reference Friday the 13th Part 8: Jason Takes Manhattan. Iridescent Boat Motor Add-on references Sweet Revenge (2025), a short film released as part of the Jason Universe Initiative. The Slasher doesn't have a face under his mask, this is due to Jason Universe never officially revealing his face. The Slasher' s lore art has a direct reference to the poster of Freddy vs. Jason, with Jason swapping position and Freddy Krueger getting replaced by The Unknown. The Slasher' s portrait render is a reference to the cover of the 1989 Friday the 13th NES game. The number 13 is used as a numerical value in aspects of all three of The Slasher' s Unique Perks, as well as large portion of his Add-Ons, as a homage to his franchise of origin, Friday The 13th. Coincidentally, the base-kit features of his Power just barely miss out on this running gag, with Omnipresent Evil' s recharge taking just 12 seconds. Whenever The Slasher is stunned, a music stinger plays:

This was added in the live release of Patch 10.0.0. The Slasher is the first truly mute Killer as he makes no sounds besides the iconic Ki Ki Ki Ma Ma Ma:

Memento Mori

The Slasher is the second Killer whose Memento Mori overrides the default Memento Mori music. The first was The Trickster 's MiNA outfit. The Slasher is the sixth Killer with a base-kit ability to kill Survivors using his Power. The Slasher is also the only Killer thus far to have more than one Mini-Mori and as such, is currently the only Killer in the game with more than two distinct Memento Mori animations. His default Mori has The Slasher eviscerate the opponent's intestines with a Hook Spike before tipping over a jerry can, creating a spark to ignite and immolate the Survivor as The Slasher watches. His first Mini-Mori, in which a Survivor is pinned to an object by a Hook Spike, has The Slasher remove the spike, pin the opponent to the object again before impaling them through the mouth with the spike. His second Mini-Mori, in which a Survivor is downed with a Hook Spike impaled in them, has The Slasher forcibly rip the spike out, ripping out the Survivor's intestines in the process.

Cosmetics

Default Outfit is taken from the Jason Universe Initiative (2023), which makes this design the main design for Jason going forward for merch, movies, games and crossovers. Backwoods Terror and Backwoods Horror are heavily inspired by his appearance in Friday the 13th Part 2, with him having hair and wearing a flannel shirt. Death Forsaken is heavily inspired by his appearance in Friday the 13th Part 6: Jason Lives with him being a skeletal zombie with gloves. Depths of Despair is heavily inspired by his appearance in Friday the 13th Part 7: The New Blood with him featuring a chain around his neck. reinforced by the Underwater Grave banner you get by purchasing the cosmetic. The color scheme seems to reference the original 1989 game. The Slasher' s cosmetic regions are erroneously split into "Head," "Torso," and "Weapon," instead of "Mask," "Torso," "Weapon." This can be identified as a mistake because it's the selected Torso piece that determines the head upon which the mask is placed, a trait shared with all other Killers that use the Mask equip region.

Lore

The Slasher crossed paths with The Unknown and Zarina Kassir. According to the flavor text to The Slasher' s teachable perks, he went to Ormond and Greenville.

power.name: Omnipresent Evil
power.description:
SPECIAL ABILITY: OMNIPRESENT EVIL Press the Secondary Power button to activate Omnipresent Evil. While activated, The Slasher is invisible, granted Undetectable and increased movement speed. The Trial Grounds also become shrouded in thick fog. You cannot see Survivors. Nearby Survivors can be sensed with Mist Clouds if they are standing still or with Footprints when they are moving. Survivors who are crouching cannot be sensed by any means. Omnipresent Evil is deactivated when performing a Jump Scare. SPECIAL ABILITY: JUMP SCARE While in Omnipresent Evil, you can target Pallets, Breakable Walls or Windows within 16 metres. Press the Secondary Power button while targetting any valid Prop to perform Jump Scare, this causes The Slasher to exit Omnipresent Evil and re-appear at the targetted location:

If the targetted prop is a dropped Pallet or a Breakable Wall, The Slasher will destroy the prop. If the targetted prop is a Window, The Slasher will vault the Window. The Window will also be blocked by the Entity for 4 seconds. If the targetted prop is a Pallet, the Pallet becomes blocked by the Entity for 4 seconds.

Press the Power button to switch the direction The Slasher will face when performing a Jump Scare. After re-appearing, The Slasher is granted 4.5454 % Haste for 25 seconds. Any Survivors within 16 metres that are being sensed by Omnipresent Evil are also revealed by Killer Instinct and scream. Performing a Jump Scare puts Omnipresent Evil on a 12 second cool-down. SPECIAL ABILITY: THROWING SPIKES The Slasher starts the Trial with a Hook Spike equipped. He can acquire them by interacting with Hooks, but doing so will destroy the Hook for some time, Hooks destroyed this way are immediately repaired when you enter Omnipresent Evil. A Hook Spike is also granted after hooking a Survivor. Regular Spikes can also be picked up by interacting with Scrap Piles scattered around the Trial Grounds. Press the Power button to aim a Spike, release the input to cancel the throw. While aiming, press Attack button to throw a Spike. When a Survivor is hit by any type of Spike, they lose 1 Health State, and are pushed forward. Survivors who collide with a pushed Survivor will be injured if healthy or affected by Deep Wound if injured. If a healthy Survivor is hit by a Hook Spike, the Spike impales into them, afflicting them with Broken until the Spike is removed. The Slasher sees the aura of the impaled Spike when close to it. If a Survivor is hit by any Spike and they enter the Dying State, colliding with a wall during the Spike impact's push causes the Survivor to be pinned into the wall. Pinned Survivors are completely immobolized, Survivors automatically un-pin themselves after some time or can be un-pinned by their fellow teammates. The Slasher is able to quickly pick up a pinned Survivor by pressing the Interaction button while next to a pinned Survivor. SPECIAL PROP: SCRAP PILES 10 Scrap Piles spawn in the Trial Grounds. Press the Interaction button while next to a Scrap Pile to pick up a regular Spike. Scrap Piles are replenished when activating Omnipresent Evil. SPECIAL INTERACTION: THROWING SPIKE KILL If a Survivor who has reached the final Hook stage or is vulnerable to a Finisher Mori is downed by any means by a Hook Spike or pinned by a regular Spike, The Slasher will be granted the ability to perform a Mini-Mori on that Survivor as long as the Survivor is still pinned/impaled.

Overview.text:
A member of the Celestial Echelon, The Judgment metes out divine punishment throughout the cosmos. When the people of Terra Primus aspired to godhood, The Judgment answered their sins with fiery retribution, razing their cities to the ground with pillars of divine light. So began a decades-long apocalypse that turned their paradise into a wasteland.

The Judgment enforces the will of The Creators with its divine light.

Its personal perks, Celestial Witness, Hex: Under Your Thumb and Lay Waste, allow it to track the Obsession, limit and surveil Survivors with Haste, and increase generator regression.

Lore.text: Recovered Fragments from the Arbiters’ Book of Letters: “Would you be counted among the heretics cleansed from this world? Or do you aspire to prove yourself to Judgment time and again, as we have proved ourselves? Then heed well these words, for their collective wisdom have saved us and, we pray, will save us still each time It returns.” (I Barbarians, ch. 3) “Some of you ask, ‘What was life before Judgment?’ Those old enough to remember dare not tell, but know that the world called Terra Primus was rife with sin and heresy. The faithless built great and terrible monuments to themselves, cities reaching into the sky, ships that pierced the heavens, and unholy machines that reached across worlds. The rulers of Terra Primus elevated themselves as gods, and in their wisdom, the Celestials sent Judgment so that we may see the error of our ways and suffer for it.” (Truths Revealed, ch. 5) “Do not seek to return to the old ways, for the towers and technologies of Terra Primus were heresy.” (Laws from Beyond, ch. 15) “Remember the settlement of Dend. Remember Lucia the Mother, who offered up her babe to Judgment and declared “great Celestial, bear witness to my devotion!” and plunged the knife into her only child. Judgment brought its light upon the people of Dend regardless, as punishment for sacrificing the innocent.” (I Barbarians, ch. 11) “Build only that which allows you to live. Sow only that which is needed to eat. To do more than this is heresy and must be punished.” (Laws from Beyond, ch. 1) “Remember that even the one who built the first shrine to Judgment was burned in Its light. Of all in the encampment, the only one spared was Koenrad the Pious, who pierced his hands upon the shrine.” (I Barbarians, ch. 12) “To worship is to suffer. Do not forget your worship but refrain from overindulging. The extent to which you must suffer is for you to discover. Anything more or less is heresy and must be punished.” (Laws from Beyond, ch. 2) “Some of you ask of the Celestials, saying ‘What is their nature? What is the order of their echelon?’ Know that their nature is unknowable, that their order is the ultimate order. Know that Judgment is the favorite of the echelon, that It represents all that is right and just across all time and all worlds.” (Truths Revealed, ch. 2) “Do not seek answers outside of Judgment, for any deviation from the will of the Gods is heresy and must be punished.” (Laws from Beyond, ch. 5) “Remember Gerhardt the Blind, who tore out his own eyes as testament to the trust he placed in Judgment. Gerhardt proved himself worthy and his death from old age was a gift from Judgment. But remember also those who followed in his example and tore out their own eyes. They were burned in Judgment’s light, as punishment for their bare-faced imitation.” (II Barbarians, ch. 7) “Fear is faith. Fear is love for Judgment. To live a life without fear is heresy, and must be punished.” (Laws from Beyond, ch. 5) “Some of you ask, ‘Why does Stardotter the Deceiver prosper? She builds beyond what is needed and stores food and wealth. She does not worship, she seeks answers in the stars. Why do her repeated heresies go unpunished while we starve and strive to see our siblings, spouses, and children burn in Judgment’s light?’ Know that Stardotter the Deceiver lives so that we may punish her, and all who follow her. This is the greatest test of our worthiness, and Judgment permits us to live so that we may triumph over her.” (Truths Revealed, ch. 3) “Look to your neighbors, and see that they are righteous in word and action. Granting mercy to heretics is itself heresy, and must be punished.” (Laws from Beyond, ch. 8) “Remember Ragnar the Traitor. Once a proud hunter of heretics, she abandoned The Arbiters and sought protection under the shadow of Stardotter the Deceiver. Protection she did not find, for when Judgment returned the following year, Ragnar was destroyed in Its light.” (III Barbarians, ch. 6) “Turn your ears away from those who followed the Deceiver. Ignore tales of black fog or dark shadows. Punish those who would talk of the Deceiver triumphing over Judgment. Engaging with the enemy’s lies is heresy and must be punished.” (Laws from Beyond, ch. 3) “Let these be the last words of The Arbiters. Judgment has not returned in twelve winters, not since It destroyed Stardotter the Deceiver. But even though our God is gone, and the heretics who call themselves Auroran have brought us low, we will never waver in our devotion. Judgment will surely return, and we will be remembered as the ones who remained faithful. It is our grim responsibility, for our children, and for our children’s children, to fight against heresy and create a new world in Judgment’s image.” (Final Testament, ch. 11)

Trivia.text:
General

The Judgment is the first original Killer entirely designed by the community as part of The Grimoire. Prior to The Judgment, The Doctor was the closest to a community-developed Killer, as his main theme was chosen by the Chinese community, drawing inspiration from a real-life figure ( Yang Yongxin ). During the Ask Me Anything - About the Grimoire! [ 1 ], Behaviour Interactive stated they considered giving The Judgment a more gender-neutral appearance, as opposed to its originally feminine concept art. They also mentioned the possibility of giving the Killer both male and female voice lines, similar to The Unknown. Ultimately It remained feminine in appearance. Due to an error on Behaviour's social media channels, the second-place design was mistakenly announced as the winner instead of the actual winning concept. The Judgment had 3 alternative names before It's name was decided by the community. The Apocalypse The Exalted The Messenger The Judgment had 3 alternative perks before the final 3 were decided by the community. Run Down the Sinner Which was a totem perk that gave incremental haste in chase. Hex: The Flesh is Weak Which was a hex perk that would have increased the exhaustion duration. Desolation Which was a perk that gave broken to survivors who were nearby and recovered from the dying state while they were inside the killer's terror radius. It is currently unknown if these perks will return in future chapters. The Judgment is the first Killer whose Power can be directly modified by the game settings.

Memento Mori

The Judgment is the third Killer whose Memento Mori overrides the default Memento Mori music. The first was The Trickster 's MiNA outfit and the second was The Slasher. The Judgment is the seventh Killer with a base-kit ability to kill Survivors using its Power. The Judgment is also the first original with the ability to Mini-Mori the Survivors, as the ability had been exclusive to a few Licensed Killers since its introduction 6 years prior.

Development

The first iteration of Ray of Retribution used to work as a laser that would follow The Judgment's hand, but it was deemed unfun and too easy to use by playtesters. The second and current iteration of Ray of Retribution functions as an Area-of-Effect laser-like attack that can be moved by killer after it spawns. It is currently under playtesting and polishing. Which is quite similar to "Pursuing Smite", an option from the grimoire before Ray of Retribution won the vote. At some point in the early stages of development, the Killer Effect went from being a progressive effect (0-100%) to a binary effect (on/off), to alleviate cognitive load as binary states are easier to understand, according to the developers in the Ask Me Anything - About the Grimoire!. The Judgment' s placeholder model used The Spirit 's Ragged Burial Kimono as body and Putrid Katana as weapon. It lacked a head model and instead used a blue flame effect. In a developer preview, the interaction to cast the Ray of Retribution was jokingly named "Woe Be Upon Ye".

power.name: Will of the Gods
power.description:
SPECIAL ABILITY: DIVINE LIGHT Press and hold the Power button to start controlling Divine Light. Release the input to stop the interaction. While controlling, a column of Divine Light appears infront of the Killer and follows the direction the Killer is facing while rapidly moving away. It does not affect Survivors during this phase. If the Killer does not cast while controlling for 3 seconds, Divine Light goes on cool-down. Press the Attack button to cast the controlled column forward. After a brief delay, it will deal damage and inflict Heresy to Survivors. Column damage delay and cast duration are improved the longer the Killer has spent controlling the column. If the column passes within 0.5 metres of a Survivor but does not hit them, they are revealed with Killer Instinct. * This can disabled/enabled in the game settings. Divine Light goes on a 6 second cool-down after casting the column forward, cancelling the casting or failing to cast in time. SPECIAL AFFLICTION: HERESY Survivors afflicted by Heresy are known as Heretics. Survivors gain Heresy by getting hit by Divine Light or by taunting The Judgment. To taunt The Judgment, the Survivor has to either:

Crouch or gesture 3 times within 10 metres Stand within an Exit Threshold for 45 seconds.

Heretics suffer from the following effects:

Can be sent to the Exile while in the Dying State While repairing Generators, Good Skill Checks will cause the Generator to regress by -3 %

If Heresy is gained while within 32 metres of an Exit Gate, it becomes blocked to the Heretic Survivor for 8 seconds. SPECIAL ABILITY: EXILE Heretics who are in the Dying State can be sent to the Exile by pressing the Secondary Power button. When sending a Survivor to the Exile, all Heretics whose Heresy is not being removed are revealed by Killer Instinct for 3 seconds The Exile acts like a Hook, Survivors who are sent to the Exile gain a Hook Stage and lose them at the same rate as being Hooked. Exile is filled with Hazards - Seeds of Punishment. If a Survivor is hit by a hazard, they lose -3 seconds of Hook Stage progress. While in Exile, Survivors are equipped with Searcher's Pendant. Survivors can point their Searcher's Pendant to collect nearby Exiled Souls. Survivors may collect up to 10 Exiled Souls. Each collected Exiled Soul extends the Unhook Protections by +0.5 seconds once rescued from the Exile. Exiled Souls do not extend Unhook Protections once all Generators have been completed. SPECIAL MODE: ZEALOUS Zealous is activated for 60 seconds after sending a Survivor to the Exile. While Zealous, the Divine Light is enhanced with the following effects:

Size increased by +10 % Cast duration increased by +50 %. Cool-down decreased by -20 %. Column control is maintained for 0.5 seconds after casting.

SPECIAL OBJECT: SHRINES OF JUDGMENT 7 Shrines of Judgment spawn in the Trial Grounds. Heretics are able to interact with a Shrine to start removing their Heresy over a period of 30 seconds. When a Survivor is Exiled, the 2 Shrines closest to The Judgment activate for Survivors. Interacting with an active Shrine will rescue Survivors inside the Exile. SPECIAL INTERACTION: HERETIC KILL Heretics who have reached the final Hook Stage can be killed while in the Dying State by pressing the Secondary Power button. This also triggers Zealous mode.

They shall be dragged through the streets in chains." — (Witness to Koenrad, ch. 41) While Zealous: Cast Divine Light will always be directed towards you. Minimum delay before cast Divine Light deals damage and inflicts Heresy is set to 0.35 seconds. Increases the maximum speed of controlled Divine Light by +100 %. Increases the maximum speed of cast Divine Light by +50 %.

addons.name: Crown of the Destroyer
addons.description: "The Creators saw this and bestowed upon It a crown and said, use this to bring light to the darkness." — (I Barbarians, ch. 6) When a Survivor is rescued from the Exile, for 20 seconds: Your Terror Radius is reduced by -70 %. Your Terror Radius is copied to all Shrines of Judgment. Grants the Undetectable Status Effect.

addons.name: Eyes of Gerhardt
addons.description: "He rapturously tore the eyes from his face after seeing such brilliant visions of the future." — (II Barbarians, ch. 60) When a Heretic completes a Generator, opens an Exit Gate or exits a Locker, all Heretics have their aura revealed for 5 seconds.

addons.name: Improvised Detonators
addons.description: "Like cowards, they strike with bombs in the night, afraid to let the light of day illuminate their blackened souls." — (Witness to Koenrad, ch. 35) If no Survivors are dead, sending a Survivor with the lowest amount of Hook States to the Exile grants +1 Token. Reaching 4 Tokens or more causes the Generator with the highest progress to explode, lose -20 % progress and start regressing.

addons.name: Mirror of the Creators
addons.description: "And They said unto It, take this mirror, and show them the error of their ways." — (I Barbarians, ch. 6) Cast Divine Light reflects off the first 2 obstructions it would otherwise pass through. When reflecting, it pauses for 0.4 seconds before reflecting again.

addons.name: Obsidian Feather
addons.description: "Some villagers will carve feathers from rocks, hoping that their faith might protect them." — (Visions of Gerhardt, ch. 3) You can no longer cancel nor manually cast the controlled Divine Light and it is automatically cast when it would instead time out. Increases movement speed while controlling Divine Light by +100 %. Decreases the maximum amount of time you can control Divine Light for by -25 %. Increases the recovery time after casting Divine Light by +10 %. Decreases the movement speed while recovering after casting Divine Light by -30 %.
